description: OpenAPI annotations, Javadoc, final CI gate, and coverage verification (T31-T34): Add @Operation/@ApiResponse/@Schema annotations to all controllers and DTOs, configure Springdoc title/version/description with disclaimer, add maven-javadoc-plugin with failOnWarnings, verify JaCoCo gates pass, confirm all @Tag("security") tests run in CI, and finalize README with badges. Independent of FEAT-003/FEAT-004 logic — purely additive documentation and CI polish. Depends on FEAT-003 and FEAT-004 being complete.
steps: Add OpenAPI annotations to g:\hsm\src\main\java\com\example\hsm\controller\KeyController.java: @Tag(name="Key Management", description="Key lifecycle operations — CryptoOfficer role required"). Each endpoint: @Operation(summary=..., description=...) with @ApiResponse entries for 200/201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 410, 422. Add @Parameter annotations on path variables and query params.

Add OpenAPI annotations to g:\hsm\src\main\java\com\example\hsm\controller\CryptoController.java: @Tag(name="Cryptographic Operations", description="Encrypt/decrypt/sign/verify — AppClient role required"). Full @ApiResponse coverage.
Add OpenAPI annotations to g:\hsm\src\main\java\com\example\hsm\controller\AuditController.java: @Tag(name="Audit Log", description="Read-only audit log access — Auditor role required").
Add OpenAPI annotations to g:\hsm\src\main\java\com\example\hsm\controller\UserController.java: @Tag(name="User Management", description="User and role management — Admin role required").

Add @Schema annotations to all DTO records/classes: description, example values, requiredMode. Ensure no @Schema example includes real key bytes or tokens — use placeholder strings like 'SGVsbG8gV29ybGQ=' for base64 examples.

Create g:\hsm\src\main\java\com\example\hsm\config\OpenApiConfig.java: @Configuration. @Bean OpenAPI customOpenAPI(): .info(new Info().title("Software HSM Emulator API").version("0.1.0").description("Educational software emulator of an HSM. NOT FIPS certified. Not for production key protection. See README for limitations.").license(new License().name("MIT"))).addSecurityItem(new SecurityRequirement().addList("BearerAuth")).components(new Components().addSecuritySchemes("BearerAuth", new SecurityScheme().type(HTTP).scheme("bearer").bearerFormat("HSM token"))).
Add springdoc configuration to application.yml: springdoc.api-docs.path=/v3/api-docs, springdoc.swagger-ui.path=/swagger-ui.html, springdoc.swagger-ui.operationsSorter=alpha.

Write integration test g:\hsm\src\test\java\com\example\hsm\controller\OpenApiTest.java extends AbstractIntegrationTest: allEndpointsAppearInApiDocs — GET /v3/api-docs, parse JSON body, assert paths contain /api/v1/keys, /api/v1/crypto/encrypt, /api/v1/crypto/decrypt, /api/v1/crypto/sign, /api/v1/crypto/verify, /api/v1/audit, /api/v1/audit/verify, /api/v1/users.

Add Javadoc comments to all public @Service class methods in: KeyService.java, CryptoService.java, AuditService.java, UserService.java, MasterKeyService.java, CryptoEngine.java, TokenService.java. Javadoc must describe parameter semantics and important security notes (e.g. 'Raw key bytes are zeroed after use'). Do NOT document the plain token value in Javadoc.
Add Javadoc to all Repository interfaces: HsmKeyRepository, HsmUserRepository, HsmKeyAclRepository, AuditRecordRepository, HsmConfigRepository.

Add maven-javadoc-plugin 3.7.0 to pom.xml (if not already added in FEAT-001): <plugin><groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId><artifactId>maven-javadoc-plugin</artifactId><version>3.7.0</version><configuration><failOnWarnings>true</failOnWarnings><doclint>all,-missing</doclint></configuration></plugin>. Run 'mvn javadoc:javadoc' to confirm zero warnings on public APIs.

Update g:\hsm\.github\workflows\ci.yml: ensure 'mvn --batch-mode verify' runs first (includes Surefire unit + Failsafe integration + JaCoCo gate), then 'mvn --batch-mode dependency-check:check'. Add step to run only @Tag("security") tests as a named step: 'mvn --batch-mode verify -Dgroups=security -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false' to confirm security tag coverage.

Verify g:\hsm\README.md is complete and accurate (it was written as a spec document — confirm it matches the implemented API paths, quick-start commands, and project structure). Update the Project Structure section if any package names or file paths changed during implementation. Add JaCoCo coverage badge placeholder: [![Coverage](./badges/jacoco.svg)](target/site/jacoco/index.html) — or use shields.io with the JaCoCo XML report endpoint.

Run 'mvn --batch-mode verify' locally from g:\hsm: confirm JaCoCo reports >= 80% line / >= 75% branch. If below threshold: identify under-covered classes, add targeted unit tests for uncovered branches (common candidates: exception handler edge cases, key state machine transitions, CryptoEngine error paths). Do NOT fake coverage with meaningless tests.
Run 'mvn --batch-mode dependency-check:check' to confirm zero HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs. If any found: upgrade the offending dependency to a patched version, re-verify.

Confirm all @Tag("security") tests appear in Surefire/Failsafe reports: check target/surefire-reports/ and target/failsafe-reports/ for test names containing the security-tagged test classes (RbacEnforcementTest, AclEnforcementTest, KeyStateGuardTest, AuditIntegrityTest, AuthenticationServiceTest, SecurityFilterTest).
Create git tag v0.1.0 on main once all CI checks pass: git tag -a v0.1.0 -m 'Initial release: software HSM emulator v0.1.0'. (Only after CI is green — do not tag if tests are failing.)
acceptance_criteria: mvn --batch-mode verify passes with BUILD SUCCESS and JaCoCo gate (line >= 80%, branch >= 75%)
mvn javadoc:javadoc produces zero warnings on public APIs
OpenApiTest#allEndpointsAppearInApiDocs passes — all 8 API paths present in /v3/api-docs
GET /swagger-ui.html loads and displays all 4 controller tag groups
mvn dependency-check:check reports zero HIGH or CRITICAL CVEs
All @Tag("security") tests appear in CI test reports (at least 25 security-tagged test methods)
README.md quick-start instructions are accurate — docker compose up -d db + export HSM_MASTER_PASSPHRASE + mvn spring-boot:run works end-to-end
git tag v0.1.0 exists on main (only after green CI)

cd g:\hsm && mvn javadoc:javadoc — zero warnings
cd g:\hsm && mvn --batch-mode verify -Dgroups=security — all security tests pass
cd g:\hsm && mvn --batch-mode dependency-check:check — zero HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs
